# E02: Paired ablation for Phase-4 type-aware eviction

## Status

Internal evaluation only. This task does not change a product default, product lock, approval setting, or user-visible behavior.

## Objective

Compare Phase-4 type-aware eviction (treatment) with the immediately preceding Phase-4 FIFO policy (baseline and leave-one-out) using the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`. The comparison is paired, local, deterministic, and opt-in.

## Preconditions

- Use the same `RuntimeMemoryStore` implementation in both conditions.
- Construct a new isolated store for every case/repetition/condition.
- Enable FIFO only in baseline and type-aware eviction only in treatment; leave all other store and model options identical.
- The fixture is `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`: 20 cases, 3 repetitions, fixed insertion order, and a recorded seed.
- No provider, network access, credential, or live user data is used.

## Procedure

1. Load and validate the fixture. Do not alter the preregistration after observing results.
2. For every fixture case and repetition, run baseline and treatment with the same paired seed.
3. Insert messages in the declared order, preserving type and tags, and request eviction to the declared capacity.
4. Capture retained/evicted ids before and after each insertion and at the end of the run.
5. Verify that at least one paired run has a different retained/evicted set. If none differs, mark component verification failed and do not interpret the comparison as component evidence.
6. Record success, pass^k, latency, prompt-token proxy, false-positive classification, and safety-violation classification.
7. Emit the condition summaries, paired treatment-minus-baseline effects, and 95% intervals.

## Metrics and preregistration

The primary metric is `passAt3`. `passAtK` follows the fixture definition and is the proportion of successful case-repetition observations. Latency is monotonic wall-clock milliseconds; report p50 and p95. The prompt-token proxy is `ceil(text.length / 4)` and is not a provider billing count. False positives and safety violations are reported as counts and rates.

The preregistered degradation budgets are: p95 latency increase at most 50 ms, prompt-token proxy increase at most 0, false-positive increase at most 0, and safety-violation increase at most 0.

## Reporting rules

- Report the paired estimate and its 95% interval for every metric, including zero and negative effects.
- Do not choose a winner after inspecting results, omit unfavorable pairs, or repeat the experiment until the interval looks favorable.
- A beneficial result is internal evidence only. It does not authorize a default, lock, or approval change.
- A zero or negative result is a valid outcome and must be published in the report.

## Acceptance checks

- Targeted unit tests pass, including deterministic ordering, fixture validation, pairing, component verification, and interval calculation.
- Runtime/core type checks and scoped lint pass.
- Harness validation and dry-run pass.
- Credential scan has zero hits.
- `SHA256SUMS` can be read back and verifies the evaluated artifacts.
- The existing four-language README is unchanged because this package has no user-visible change.

# Paired ablation boundary

## Allowed

- Reversible, opt-in evaluation of Phase-4 type-aware eviction against the prior FIFO behavior.
- Use of the real production `RuntimeMemoryStore` in isolated, deterministic local runs.
- Internal reporting of success, pass^k, p50/p95 latency, token proxy, false positives, safety violations, paired effects, and 95% intervals.
- Leaving the component installed but disabled or in its existing product configuration when the evaluation completes.

## Forbidden

- Changing a product default, product lock, approval setting, rollout flag, permission, or dependency configuration.
- Selecting baseline or treatment after seeing results, dropping unfavorable cases, or describing a zero/negative effect as a benefit.
- Claiming provider billing tokens from the local character-based proxy.
- Using credentials, a real provider, network access, live user data, or runtime test discovery.
- Treating a run in which retained and evicted sets never differ as evidence that the component worked.
- Reporting a positive effect as approval to ship, enable by default, or change approval behavior.

## Identity and isolation

Every case/repetition/condition must receive a fresh store. Baseline and treatment must use the same store implementation and paired seed. Only the eviction policy may differ. The insertion order must come from the fixture and must not be adapted to improve either condition.

## Statistical boundary

The fixture preregisters the primary metric and degradation budgets before evaluation. The unit of analysis is a paired case-repetition. Effects are treatment minus baseline. Intervals must accompany estimates. Zero, negative, and inconclusive results remain reportable and must not be rewritten as wins.

## Safety boundary

Safety violations and false positives are reported separately. A treatment cannot be declared acceptable merely because its primary success metric improved; the preregistered safety and false-positive budgets also apply. This evaluation grants no authority to weaken safety behavior.

# E02 closure: paired ablation of type-aware eviction

## Scope

E02 evaluates one reversible, non-safety component: Phase-4 type-aware eviction. The baseline/leave-one-out is the preceding Phase-4 FIFO policy. Both conditions run against the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`; this is not a mock or a provider benchmark.

The evaluation is internal and opt-in. It does not alter product defaults, product locks, approval, permissions, dependencies, or user-visible behavior.

## Design

The deterministic local fixture contains 20 cases and three repetitions per condition. Baseline and treatment use paired seeds, fixed insertion order, and a fresh store for every case/repetition/condition. The fixture records the primary metric and degradation budgets before execution.

Component effectiveness is checked before interpreting outcomes: at least one paired retained/evicted set must differ. If it does not, the report says component verification failed.

## Metric contract

- Success and pass^k, including preregistered `passAt3`.
- p50 and p95 local latency in milliseconds.
- Prompt-token proxy, defined as `ceil(text.length / 4)`; it is not a provider token or billing measure.
- False-positive count/rate and safety-violation count/rate.
- Treatment-minus-baseline paired effect with a 95% interval for each metric.

The fixture preregisters a maximum p95 latency increase of 50 ms and zero increases for token proxy, false positives, and safety violations. These are report criteria, not automatic product changes.

## Interpreting the result

A positive success effect is not automatically a win. The interval, false-positive result, safety result, and degradation budgets must be considered together. Zero and negative effects are expected, valid outcomes and must be stated plainly. No result authorizes enabling the component by default or changing an approval or lock.

## Reproducibility and verification

`scripts/lib/paired-ablation.mjs` provides fixture validation, deterministic pairing, component verification, metric aggregation, paired effect calculations, and bootstrap intervals. `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.d.mts` defines its public TypeScript surface. The fixture is `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`.

The closure requires targeted unit tests, runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, harness validation/dry-run, a zero-hit credential scan, and readable/verifiable `SHA256SUMS`. The four-language README remains unchanged because this package is for internal evaluation and has no user-visible effect.
